settings.heading: Step 1: Preparation (2-3 hours)
settings.row_content: Unbox your kit, inventory all parts against the checklist, and watch the introductory video tutorials. Familiarise yourself with the tools and materials before starting.

settings.heading: Step 2: Jig Assembly (4-6 hours)
settings.row_content: Assemble the plywood alignment jig and set it to your chosen geometry. Prepare the bamboo tubes by checking fit and making any final adjustments.

settings.heading: Step 3: Bonding (8-12 hours)
settings.row_content: The main build phase. Join the bamboo tubes with epoxy resin and wrap the joints with carbon fibre tow. This is where your frame takes shape.

settings.heading: Step 4: Curing (24-48 hours)
settings.row_content: Let the epoxy fully cure at room temperature. No work needed — just patience. This ensures maximum joint strength.

settings.heading: Step 5: Finishing (6-10 hours)
settings.row_content: Sand the joints smooth, apply protective sealant to the bamboo, and install your headset and bottom bracket. Your frame is ready for components!

settings.caption: Most builders spread this over 2-4 weekends
settings.heading: Build Timeline

settings.text:
8-12 years lifespan · <1% failure rate · 28,000 PSI tensile strength

Bamboo's natural flexibility absorbs road vibration better than metal or carbon fibre, giving you a smoother, more comfortable ride. Tested with Swansea University. Builders have toured continents and raced on bamboo frames built from our kits.

settings.heading: Do I need special tools?
settings.row_content: No power tools required. Basic hand tools: hacksaw, files, sandpaper, measuring tape, and a work surface. Everything else is included in the kit.

settings.heading: What if I make a mistake?
settings.row_content: Most mistakes are fixable. Epoxy can be sanded and re-applied. Bamboo is forgiving. If you're stuck, our community forum has seen every problem — someone will have the answer within hours.

settings.heading: What else do I need to complete the bike?
settings.row_content: Fork, wheels, groupset, handlebars, saddle, and finishing components. We offer component packs with everything included, or you can source parts from any bike shop.

settings.heading: How strong is bamboo?
settings.row_content: 28,000 PSI tensile strength — comparable to steel. Tested with Swansea University. Builders tour continents and race on them.
